# cooonfig

> cooonfig builds one YAML model from ordered model templates, then renders that model through output templates into config files. Model templates see named inputs and the model so far (`.model`). Output templates see only the finished model.

Read this file before writing `cooonfig.yaml`, input YAML, model templates, or output templates. `example/` shows the pipeline: named inputs, ordered model files, then one output template per file. Those example templates often print strings unquoted; follow the quoting rules below when writing new templates. Sprig text functions are available in every template: https://masterminds.github.io/sprig/

## Run

```bash
cooonfig --config example/cooonfig.yaml --input-dir example --output-dir target
```

From a checkout: `go run ./cmd/cooonfig --config example/cooonfig.yaml --input-dir example --output-dir target`.

| Flag | Short | Default | Paths in the config |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config` | `-c` | `./cooonfig.yaml` | — |
| `--input-dir` | `-i` | `./` | `inputs[].path` |
| `--output-dir` | `-o` | `./` | `outputs[].outfile` |

`models[]` and `outputs[].template` are relative to the directory that contains the config file, not `--input-dir`. Output parent directories are created. Existing output files are truncated. There are no subcommands; extra positional arguments print help. `--version` / `-v` prints the version. Errors go to stderr as `Error: ...` and the process exits 1. Stdout lines (`read config`, `read input`, `read model`, `render output`) are progress logs. The generated files are the result.

`inputs`, `models`, and `outputs` are all required and must be non-empty.

```yaml
inputs:
  - name: app
    path: application.yaml
  - name: env
    path: environment.yaml
    type: yaml
models:
  - models/core.yaml
  - models/default.yaml
outputs:
  - template: templates/apache_config.json
    outfile: apache/config.json
```

Each input needs `name` and `path`. `type` defaults to `yaml` and `yaml` is the only accepted type. Names must be unique. The name `model` is reserved.

## Pipeline

1. Read each input as plain YAML. Inputs are not templates. `{{ }}` in an input is data, not a directive.
2. Render each model template in order with Go `text/template`. Parse the rendered text as one YAML mapping. Deep-merge it into the model.
3. Render each output template against the finished model and write the bytes as-is. Output text is not parsed as YAML.

Input files and each rendered model must be a YAML mapping (top-level keys). A top-level list or scalar fails unmarshalling. Empty output, comments only, or `null` add no keys. A model file is a single YAML document; only the first document is read.

Deep-merge rules, applied after each model template:

- Nested maps merge recursively.
- Any other value at the same key replaces the previous value. A later list replaces the earlier list. A scalar replaces a map, and a map replaces a scalar.
- Keys are never deleted. Omitting a key from a later model leaves the earlier value in place. Writing `null` stores nil; it does not remove the key.
- The template sees `.model` as it existed before this file. Keys produced by the current file are visible only to later model templates, under `.model`, and to output templates as root fields.

## Who sees what

Model template data:

- `.app`, `.env`, and any other input name: that input's YAML mapping.
- `.model`: the map merged from earlier model templates. It is empty for the first model.
- `$`: the same root. Inside `with` or `range`, `.` changes and `$` is the way back to inputs and `.model`.

Output template data:

- `.` is the finished model. Print `.app_name`, not `.model.app_name` and not `.app.name`.
- Input names are not in scope. Copy every value an output needs onto the model in a model template.
- `$` is the finished model.

```yaml
# models/core.yaml — inputs and the model so far
app_name: {{ .app.name | quote }}
app_url: {{ required ".app.source.url is required" .app.source.url | quote }}
```

```yaml
# models/default.yaml — later model, reads earlier keys
working_directory: {{ printf "./workspace/%s" .model.app_name | quote }}
```

```json
{
  "ApplicationName": {{ .app_name | toJson }},
  "WorkingDirectory": {{ .working_directory | toJson }}
}
```

A missing map key does not fail rendering. `{{ .app.missing }}` and `{{ .missing.child }}` print the literal `<no value>`. YAML then stores that as the string `"<no value>"`, and output files contain it too. Guard required fields with `required` or `fail` so a bad input stops the run.

## Model templates

Model templates are the contract between inputs and outputs. Compute defaults, paths, and validation here. Leave output templates as formatting.

- Emit a YAML mapping of the keys you want to add or override.
- Prefer one file per concern, ordered from required facts, to defaults, to environment overrides. See `example/models/core.yaml`, `default.yaml`, and `kubernetes.yaml`.
- Quote strings with Sprig `quote`. Unquoted text breaks or changes type when it is parsed back as YAML. `hello: world` is a mapping error. `1.10` becomes float `1.1`. `01` becomes int `1`. `true` / `false` become booleans. An unquoted timestamp such as `2024-01-02` becomes a timestamp. `0.1.0` stays a string only because it is not a valid float. `quote` keeps the characters you wrote.
- Print numbers and booleans without `quote` when the output really wants those types.
- Do not print a map or list with bare `{{ .model.ports }}`. Go formatting produces `map[a:1]` and `[80 443]`, which is invalid YAML. Use `toYaml`, `toJson`, or `range`.
- Do not render `{{ . | toYaml }}` or `{{ toYaml .model }}` as the model body. `.` includes the inputs and `.model`. Emit only the keys this file is responsible for.
- `toYaml` sorts map keys, indents nested collections four spaces, and ends with a newline. Put the action at column 0 and indent with `nindent`:

```yaml
source:
{{ .app.source | toYaml | nindent 2 }}
```

- Build nested values in the template, then marshal them, so quoting is not done by hand:

```yaml
server:
{{ dict "host" .env.host "port" .env.port | toYaml | nindent 2 }}
```

- Lists replace. To add an item, write the whole list again. `append` on a missing list fails; use `default (list)` first:

```yaml
ports:
{{ append (.model.ports | default (list)) .env.extra_port | toYaml | nindent 2 }}
```

- Keys that are not identifiers (`app-name`, `01ver`) are read with `index`: `{{ index .app "app-name" | quote }}`.
- `{{ define "partial" }}` and `{{ template "partial" . }}` work only inside the same file. There is no shared partial library and no `include`.

Validate in the model that first needs the value:

```yaml
{{ if not .app.name }}
{{ fail "app.name is required" }}
{{ end }}
app_name: {{ .app.name | quote }}
app_version: {{ .app.version | default "0.1.0" | quote }}
```

`fail` aborts rendering. `if not` and Sprig `default` / `empty` treat nil, `false`, `0`, `""`, and empty maps or lists as empty, so `default` will replace a real `0` or `false`. `required` is stricter about type and looser about other empties: it errors only for nil or `""`, and it accepts `0` and `false`.

## Output templates

Output templates may be JSON, YAML, env files, XML, or any other text. cooonfig does not check the format. Invalid JSON is still written if the template emits it.

- Every field printed here must already exist on the model. Shared defaults belong in a model template so every output sees them.
- A missing key prints `<no value>` and still writes the file. Call `required` on fields the file cannot do without: `{{ required "app_name is required" .app_name }}`.
- `quote` is for YAML scalars. For JSON strings use `toJson`, which adds quotes and escapes. Do not wrap `toJson` in extra quotes.

```json
{
  "ApplicationName": {{ required "app_name is required" .app_name | toJson }},
  "Port": {{ .port }}
}
```

- A whole document can be dumped for debugging, as in `example/templates/all.json` and `all.yaml`: `{{ . | toPrettyJson }}` and `{{ . | toYaml }}`.
- Hand-write a different shape when the output schema is not the model schema, as in `example/templates/kafka_config.yml` and `apache_config.json`.
- Inside `with` or `range`, `.` is the current value. Use `$` for other model fields: `{{ $.app_name }}`.
- `text/template` does not HTML-escape. `&` and `<` are written unchanged.
- To emit the characters `{{` or `}}`, print them as strings: `{{ "{{" }}` and `{{ "}}" }}`.
- Sprig `toYaml` is not defined by Sprig. cooonfig provides `toYaml`. Sprig does provide `toJson`, `toPrettyJson`, and `toRawJson`.

## Functions

Templates use Sprig's text function map, plus two cooonfig functions. Both argument orders work; the piped value is the last argument.

`required` — message first, value second. Errors when the value is nil or `""`:

```
{{ required ".app.source.url is required" .app.source.url }}
{{ .app.source.url | required ".app.source.url is required" }}
```

`toYaml` — marshal one value to YAML (sorted keys, four-space nested indent, trailing newline).

Sprig functions used most often from this tool:

| Function | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `fail` | Abort with a message: `{{ fail "app.name is required" }}` |
| `default` | Replace an empty value. Also replaces `0` and `false`. |
| `empty` | Test for empty, including `0` and `false`. |
| `quote` / `squote` | Quote a YAML string. |
| `nindent` / `indent` | Indent marshaled YAML. `nindent` starts with a newline. |
| `toJson` / `toPrettyJson` | JSON values and documents. |
| `dict` / `list` / `append` / `hasKey` / `index` / `dig` | Build and read maps and lists. |
| `printf` | Assemble strings before quoting. |

`dig` takes keys, then a default, then the map: `{{ dig "source" "url" "" .app }}`.

## Checklist

- Config has non-empty `inputs`, `models`, and `outputs`. No input is named `model`. Every input `type` is omitted or `yaml`.
- Input paths are relative to `--input-dir`. Model and output template paths are relative to the config file's directory. `outfile` is relative to `--output-dir`.
- Each input file is a YAML mapping.
- Each model template renders one YAML mapping. Strings are passed through `quote`. Maps and lists are passed through `toYaml`.
- Required inputs use `required` or `fail`. The rendered model never contains `<no value>`.
- Later models override by writing the same key. They do not expect list merge or key deletion.
- Output templates read root model fields only. JSON strings use `toJson`.
- Run cooonfig and read the files under `--output-dir`.
